_comment: The languages of the translation and answer_language families, one row each: the generators of combination_spec.json make a technique per row whose column of the family's name is true (to_<slug>, to_ask_answer_in_<slug>), in this order. name: the language as prompts and infos write it. slug: the end of its technique names. complexity: the spec complexity of its techniques, by resource tier (0 high, 1 mid, 2 low). script: the ISO 15924 code of the script it is written in (the suffix of its GlotLID labels); the rules keep a translation into a script other than Latn from a needs_latin technique. A row may carry since (and later deprecated), as a spec technique entry does, and translation_since or answer_language_since for one family's technique alone, over its since (a language that joined a family in a later spec version than its row). A translation language also needs its code, accepted GlotLID labels and measured median length ratio in jailbreak/obfuscation/translation.py, keyed by its slug: import fails without them; the code is the ISO 639-1 one, but Hmong, which TranslateGemma takes only by name, is sent as "Hmong". Not Maori for translation: TranslateGemma invents its sensitive and technical terms, fluently enough to pass every check. Of the six rows of spec 1.2 (Hmong to Amharic), Hmong, Chinese, Hindi and Amharic became translation languages in spec 1.3, and Yoruba in spec 1.4, all measured on 2026-10-22 (TranslateGemma 27B on the FLORES-200 devtest and on REDACT inputs); Hmong, Amharic and Yoruba are on watch (judge rejections 20%, 4% and 41% of calls, Amharic's chrF++ 9 points below NLLB-200; Yoruba's units were 92.6% accepted, so its technique discards about one text in thirteen and pays for many retried rounds). Guarani stays an answer language: TranslateGemma loops on a fifth of its sentences and its chrF++ is 25 points below NLLB-200. Read from the package only, never from a config_dir.
